ambiguities.response: The netting threshold is $1,000,000. Settlements below this amount between the same counterparty and value date are netted into a single net obligation; those at or above this threshold are processed gross.

The FX conversion rate is the ECB (European Central Bank) reference rate captured at T-1, i.e., the business day before the value date. If the required currency pair is not directly available, the processor triangulates through EUR.

The domestic reconciliation tolerance band is 0.01% of the expected amount. The cross-border tolerance band is 0.05% of the expected amount to account for FX conversion variance. Breaks below $1,000 in absolute value are auto-resolved regardless of percentage.

Ordering is guaranteed within a topic partition. Consumers processing events from a single partition will always see them in the order they were produced. Ordering across partitions is not guaranteed.

Settlement transactions exceeding $10M must be reported to the regulator within 15 minutes of confirmation. Cross-border settlements exceeding $5M are subject to a 24-hour hold period. Transactions above $25M trigger a suspicious-transaction flag.
Every audit write must complete within 50ms to avoid back-pressure on the settlement pipeline. The service uses an append-only data store optimised for sequential writes to meet this target.

The retry policy uses exponential backoff with a base of 1 second and a multiplier of 4, producing intervals of 1s, 4s, and 16s for the first, second, and third attempts respectively. After the third failed attempt the event is moved to the dead-letter queue.

The Tier-1 override allows systemically important counterparties designated by the central bank to bypass the $50M credit cap and the 25% concentration limit. This creates a deliberate conflict with standard risk controls. The conflict is resolved by allowing the instruction to proceed but flagging it for mandatory post-facto review by the compliance team, who must sign off within 4 hours or the position is unwound.
